facts.text: Brookneal was founded in 1802 as a ferry crossing on the Staunton River, chosen by Patrick Henry to link Campbell, Halifax, and Charlotte counties.
The town’s name honors John Brooke and his wife Sarah Neal, whose tobacco warehouse became known as “Brooke’s Warehouse.”.
In 1887 the Lynchburg and Durham Railroad began construction through Brookneal, later becoming part of the Virginian Railway in 1907.
Red Hill, Patrick Henry’s plantation, now operates as a historic museum and National Memorial just outside Brookneal.
The Staunton River’s historic sluices and falls once powered bateaux that carried tobacco from Brookneal plantations to distant markets.
Brookneal’s recreation park features a boat ramp on the Staunton River, a nod to the town’s long river‑transport heritage.
